verdict.rationale: Outlook's own mail docs say messages can be filtered, searched, or sorted across specific folders or the entire mailbox, and that queries can populate search folders, which covers the core of searching full mail history. This evidence is API-level, though, not a description of the end-user search experience. One community user found searching via an LLM integration faster than Outlook's web search field, which weakens the 'fast' claim without concretely contradicting a documented capability. Missing for 10: documented search operators/syntax, relevance-ranked results, evidence of speed, and hands-on confirmation of precise search in the client UI.

support.subject: As a power-user, search is fast and precise — operators, filters, and ranked results across my full mail history

citations.quote: Apps can conveniently [filter, search, or sort](query-parameters) messages in specific folders or the user's entire mailbox.
